summary: Frontend-only validation of the playlist persistence fix in /app/frontend/app/utils/playlistStorage.ts (dual-write to AsyncStorage + file backup on native, safe no-op on web, auto-recovery when AsyncStorage empty). Static code review + web-runtime functional tests all PASS. Persistence across reload works via localStorage on web. No resurrection after delete verified via LS-empty simulation. Regression on rename, playback, MiniPlayer, and all 5 tabs is clean. NOTE: The native file backup path (documentDirectory/playlists_backup.json via expo-file-system/legacy) cannot be exercised in the browser preview - verified via code review only. Deprecated package warnings previously reported (expo-av, non-route files under app/, textShadow/shadow/pointerEvents/resizeMode style deprecations) still present, unrelated to this fix.

react_native_issues.issue: Deprecated: expo-av should be migrated to expo-audio (audio) and expo-video (video) per Expo SDK 54. Console warning on every render. Reference: /app/frontend/package.json:23 and /app/frontend/app/contexts/AudioPlayerContext.tsx (pre-existing, not introduced by this fix)

Utility/context/constant/component files placed under app/ trigger 'missing default export' warnings for AddToPlaylistModal.tsx, MiniPlayer.tsx, musicData.ts, AudioPlayerContext.tsx, playlistStorage.ts, shareTrack.ts, etc. Non-fatal but pollutes logs. Recommend moving out of app/. (pre-existing)

action_items: None required for the persistence fix - it is correct and passes all web-testable acceptance criteria. Ship it.
OPTIONAL (unchanged from prior iterations): migrate expo-av to expo-audio/expo-video, and move non-route files out of app/ directory to silence expo-router warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: playlistStorage.ts BACKUP_FILE guard: `Platform.OS !== 'web' && FileSystem.documentDirectory` correctly makes web a full no-op (writeBackup/readBackup return early when BACKUP_FILE is null). GOOD.

savePlaylists always writes to backup AFTER AsyncStorage.setItem (even inside a try/catch that only catches the AsyncStorage error). Backup writes even when AsyncStorage throws, which is the exact recovery scenario we want. GOOD.

getPlaylists recovery only fires when AsyncStorage is truly empty/unreadable (`data` is null OR `playlists.length === 0`). Won't overwrite legitimate empty state on native because when user has deleted all playlists, savePlaylists([]) has already written '[]' to the backup file, so readBackup returns [] and `backup.length > 0` is false. NO RESURRECTION. GOOD.

deletePlaylist -> filter -> savePlaylists(filtered): if filtered is [], both AsyncStorage and backup file get overwritten with []. Verified by simulating LS='[]' on web: 'No playlists yet' shown after reload. GOOD.
All CRUD functions (create/rename/delete/addTrack/removeTrack/getPlaylistById) route through getPlaylists() so the recovery seed happens on ANY read. GOOD.
expo-file-system import uses '/legacy' subpath which is the correct API for FileSystem.writeAsStringAsync/readAsStringAsync/getInfoAsync in SDK 54 (expo-file-system 19+). GOOD.
app.json expo-build-properties -> android.allowBackup:true correctly set (enables Google Auto Backup as a 3rd layer of defense across uninstall/reinstall). GOOD.
seed_data_creation: Seeded LS 'user_playlists' with test playlist during runtime; cleared before each test run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Top tab bar (Home/Search/Library/Favorites/Profile) is at y<100, height<40 - use JS-based tab clicks with a y filter to disambiguate from screen-body text. RN Alert.alert on the web preview does NOT render as native window.confirm (Playwright's dialog handler cannot dismiss it), and the buttons ('Delete', 'Cancel') are rendered inside an off-tree overlay that is hard to locate. rca_of_issue: This iteration validates a BUG FIX, not a new feature. Root cause per E1's analysis: on some Android devices, the AsyncStorage SQLite database (RKStorage) can be corrupted/cleared during Play Store app updates, wiping playlists that were saved locally. The fix implements defense-in-depth: (1) DUAL-WRITE - every savePlaylists also writes /documentDirectory/playlists_backup.json via expo-file-system/legacy on native; (2) AUTO-RECOVERY - getPlaylists falls back to the backup file and re-seeds AsyncStorage whenever the primary is empty/unreadable; (3) app.json now sets android.allowBackup:true so Google Auto Backup preserves data across uninstall/reinstall as a third safety net. Verification: (a) Static review confirms the dual-write and recovery logic is correct and cannot resurrect deleted playlists because deletePlaylist->savePlaylists([]) overwrites the backup with an empty array. (b) Web runtime tests confirm PersistTest playlist created via UI persists across full page reload with the added track (localStorage-backed on web). (c) Simulating post-delete state (LS='[]' or LS removed) after reload shows 'No playlists yet' - no resurrection. (d) Regression tests confirm rename, playback (MiniPlayer visible), and all 5 tabs work without crashes.
